prompt: In Microsoft Word, which tab is used first when a user wants to change page orientation from portrait to landscape?
rationale: Orientation lives under Layout because it controls page setup.

prompt: A student wants to send the same letter to many recipients using names from a list. Which Word tab should they open first?
rationale: Mail merge tools sit on the Mailings tab.

prompt: A worksheet must print on one page wide. Which area should the user use first in Excel?
rationale: Scale to Fit controls width and page fitting.

prompt: If a formula must keep the tax rate cell fixed when copied down, what should be used?
rationale: Absolute referencing locks the source cell during copying.

prompt: Which command should be used if the paper says 'use a function to count cells that meet a condition'?
rationale: COUNTIF counts cells matching a specific rule.

prompt: Which sequence best matches the information processing cycle tested in N5?
rationale: The standard sequence is input, processing, output, then storage.

prompt: The paper says 'Save the document in your examination folder as REPORT_1'. Which action best follows that instruction?
options: Use Save As and type REPORT_1 in the required folder
Print the document first and rename the hard copy
Close the file and hope autosave keeps the right name
Create a shortcut on the desktop
rationale: Save As is the controlled method for creating the required file name in the correct folder.

prompt: If the exam says 'move the file', what should happen after the action is completed correctly?
options: The file exists in the new folder only
The file exists in both folders
rationale: Move transfers the file to the new location instead of copying it.

prompt: A heading must appear automatically in a table of contents later in the document. Which method is correct?
options: Apply a heading style to the heading text
Make the heading bold and larger manually
Press Enter several times above the heading
Insert the heading inside a text box
rationale: Automatic document structures depend on styles, not manual appearance only.

prompt: The paper says 'apply 1.5 line spacing to the body text only'. What must the learner control carefully?
options: Select the correct text range before changing spacing
Change the whole document and hope it is accepted
Use Enter after every line instead
Insert a page break before the body text
rationale: The instruction limits the change to a specific part of the document.

prompt: A question says 'display the answer to 2 decimals'. Which statement is correct?
options: Formatting changes appearance; rounding changes the stored value
Formatting and rounding always do exactly the same thing
Decimals are controlled from the Data tab
rationale: Spreadsheet marks are lost when students confuse number formatting with real rounding.

prompt: The task says to transfer evidence from one subtask into another. What protects the marks best?
options: Verify file names, paths, and the exact required output before moving on
Rename everything at the end if there is time
Paste random screenshots to show effort
Ignore the evidence instruction if the main answer is correct
rationale: Integration marks depend on controlled transfer, not partial completion in isolation.

prompt: A question asks about synchronous online communication between participants in real time. Which term fits best?
rationale: Synchronous tools operate live in the same session.

prompt: When a task asks for collaborative cloud note sharing, what must the student verify first?
rationale: Cloud collaboration fails immediately when access rights are wrong.

prompt: Which sequence best matches the required intervention discipline for a timed N6 task?
rationale: The intervention engine keeps the same fixed sequence across streams.

prompt: In an advanced N6 Word task, what is the strongest reason to prefer the correct layout tool over manual spacing?
options: Because the paper rewards controlled method and stable output, not visual guesswork
Because manual spacing always creates automatic styles
Because the examiner ignores layout method
Because spacing makes print settings irrelevant
rationale: N6 practical work still punishes method weakness even when the page looks acceptable at first glance.

prompt: A spreadsheet task requires a chart that stays readable in print. What should the learner verify?
options: Titles, labels, and output layout before final lock
Whether the workbook name is short
Whether the chart was moved with the mouse
rationale: Chart and output readability are mark-bearing presentation controls in higher practical work.

prompt: Why is print/output checking more important in advanced practical work than students often assume?
options: Because layout, chart, and structure marks can still be lost after the main content is finished
Because print settings replace formula checking
Because output no longer matters at N6
rationale: Advanced practical marks still depend on the final output behaving correctly.

prompt: A task asks for non-contiguous selection before charting. What is being tested most directly?
rationale: N6 practical work often checks whether learners can manipulate data structures deliberately.

prompt: What is the safest response when an N6 practical instruction is very specific about format and placement?
options: Follow the wording exactly and verify the output against it
Ignore the placement if the content is right
Use a screenshot instead of the required live object
rationale: Specific wording defines the mark-bearing deliverable and should not be creatively reinterpreted.

prompt: Why is notebook organisation a mark-bearing issue in N6 rather than a personal preference?
options: Because evidence, sequence, and retrievability affect later tasks and lecturer judgement
Because notebook work never connects to the paper
Because neatness only matters for attendance
Because notebook tools replace all theory
rationale: The notebook workflow is part of controlled task execution, not just visual tidiness.

prompt: What is the practical difference between synchronous and asynchronous communication in workflow tasks?
options: Synchronous happens in real time; asynchronous allows delayed response
Synchronous is always offline; asynchronous is always face-to-face
rationale: N6 communication theory should support correct platform and workflow decisions.

prompt: The task asks the learner to capture, store, and reuse evidence across subtasks. What is being tested most directly?
rationale: Evidence handling becomes part of the wider integration workflow in N6.

prompt: If a learner produces the right-looking output through the wrong method in the mock, what remains true?
options: Method weakness still matters because the exam rewards controlled execution
The method never matters if the result looks right
Wrong method improves the rubric score
rationale: A paper-backed mock should still reflect method-sensitive marking logic.
